prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

Title, set largest at the top left of the page: pipeline
Deck beneath it: The mill itself — every essay steps one station forward each cycle, from waiting idea to checked draft, while the overseer's board shows the whole floor at once.

Hero: a long mill floor drawn in gentle perspective, five work stations in a row joined by a walking beam overhead, labeled in order on small hanging shingles: pending, research, outline, draft, factcheck, and at the row's end a filled shelf labeled done. Essays are drawn as paper folders moving along the line, several on the floor at once at different stations — one waiting at pending, one open under a reading lamp at research, one being ruled into headings at outline, one thickening under a pen at draft, one held against a candling light at factcheck, a small stack resting at done. A note above the beam: each turn of the beam advances an essay one station; the beam turns on its own, every few seconds.

Above and behind the floor, the overseer's gallery: a large wall board drawn as a clean panel of small tiles, one tile per essay, arranged in columns matching the stations below, a few tiles marked with small sums. Beside the board, a modest lever set to a notch labeled paused, with a note: the mill wakes up paused; the overseer releases the lever to begin, may step the beam by hand, or slow its turning.

Two quiet details along the bottom:
- lower left: one station's lamp gone dark with a small card propped against it reading trying again, captioned — when the far-off model does not answer, the mill waits and retries; nothing is lost;
- lower right: a folder's inside cover shown open, its stage stamps and a small running cost figure visible, captioned — every essay carries its own state on paper; the mill can stop and resume mid-book.

One warm accent colour follows the folders along the line and their tiles on the board; the mill frame, beam, and gallery stay in ink.
